raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through for the year ahead.

---

My family has 5 mu, which isn't much — some folks in the village have 20 or 30 mu, and the big operators nearby have hundreds. So every yuan I spend on inputs matters. My wife and I do most of the field work ourselves, and our oldest helps out during busy times when school's out. I've been doing wheat-maize rotation since I took over from my father, and honestly I don't see much reason to change the system — it's what works here, and the ground is set up for it.

**Winter wheat (just harvested in June, so I'm planning the next round for this October):**

I'll plant around October 10-15, same as always. Last year I sowed a little late because of rain and the yield suffered a bit, so I want to be on time this year. I buy seed from the agricultural supply store in the township — the extension guy recommended Jimai 22 a few years back and most of us in the village use it or Shimai. About 15 kg of seed per mu, costs maybe 50 yuan per mu.

For fertilizer, I do the usual two-step: a compound fertilizer at sowing (15-15-15, about 40 kg per mu as the base), then topdress urea at jointing around March if the wheat looks like it needs it. Usually I end up putting about 16-17 kg of nitrogen per mu total across the season. The extension station said 15 is enough but I've found wheat looks better with a bit more — and urea isn't that expensive. I can't afford to come up short after spending all winter waiting for it.

Irrigation: I'll give it one good watering before winter to help it through the cold, then one at jointing and one at grain filling. Three times should do it unless spring is really dry. The well pump costs me around 40 yuan per mu per watering with electricity.

For pests and weeds, I spray herbicide once in early spring for broadleaf weeds, and watch for aphids near heading — I'll only spray insecticide if I see them, no sense spending money otherwise. My neighbor Old Wang got hit by fusarium two years ago so I might do a preventive fungicide at flowering if the weather turns humid.

Expected yield: around 430 kg/mu is what I usually get. Some years 470, some years 380.

**Summer maize (plant right after wheat harvest in June):**

This is the tight part of the year. Wheat comes off around June 10-12, and I need maize in the ground by June 15 at the latest or the growing season gets too short. I don't own a no-till planter — I hire the machine operator who comes through the village, costs about 30 yuan/mu to direct-drill maize into the wheat stubble. No real tillage, just drill it in. That's what most people do now.

I use a hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the dealer has — about 2 kg per mu, 60 yuan or so per mu. 

Fertilizer: I broadcast compound fertilizer at planting (another 40 kg/mu of 15-15-15) and then topdress urea once at big-flare stage (around V10-V12), maybe 15 kg of urea per mu. Total nitrogen ends up around 15 kg/mu. Maize is thirstier for N than wheat but I do less because we usually get summer rain here.

Irrigation: maybe once or twice if July-August stays dry. If there's good rain I skip it entirely and save the pumping money.

Pesticide: herbicide at planting (post-emergence spray about 2 weeks in), and I watch for corn borer — usually spray once in July if the trap shows them coming.

Expected yield: around 480 kg/mu.

---

My main worries this year: diesel and fertilizer prices have been creeping up, and the grain procurement price hasn't really kept up. If fertilizer goes up another 10% I might cut back the topdress on maize a little. The other thing is my daughter starts middle school in the fall and we need cash for that, so I'm not going to experiment with any new varieties or inputs this year — sticking with what I know works.
